   - **The whole lock diff, expected** — one line added in escher-driver's `dependencies` list (`Cargo.lock:3209-3218`
     at `239c197c1`), nothing else:
     ```
     @@ escher-driver's dependencies = [ … ]
       "serde_json",
     + "skrifa",
       "tracing",
     ```
     `git diff --numstat 239c197c1 -- Cargo.lock` reads `1	0	Cargo.lock`.
   - /implement records the diff it measured, whole, in `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-24-canvas-lint/evidence/lock-diff.md`
     (its hunk, its numstat), then fires the `--locked` workspace build entry (`ci-leg.sh build`, `cargo build
     --workspace --locked`). A lock diff that differs from the one above, by any line, is a stop: the step reports the
     diff and asks the operator. It is never trimmed by hand.

2. **The label reading** (new `packages/escher-driver/src/canvas_lint.rs`, its unit tests in the `#[path]` child
   `canvas_lint_tests.rs`, arch S4).
   - `pub(crate) struct Label` holds two rectangles in the scene's device px:
     - `ink` — the run's ink box;
     - `clip` — the box its enclosing pushes leave, or `None` where no push encloses it.
   - `pub(crate) fn labels(commands: &[RenderCommand]) -> Vec<Label>` walks the recorded commands in paint order:
     - A stack of clip boxes. `PushLayer`, `PushClipLayer` and `PushMaskLayer` each push their clip path's bounding
       box, mapped through the push's own transform, cut to the box beneath it on the stack. `PopLayer` pops one;
       a pop on an empty stack changes nothing.
     - Each `GlyphRun` yields one `Label` whose `clip` is the stack's top, where its ink box is not empty.
   - `fn ink(run)` reads the run's font through `skrifa::FontRef::from_index(run.font_data.data.data(),
     run.font_data.index)`, then `glyph_metrics(Size::new(run.font_size), LocationRef::new(..))` at the run's own
     normalized coordinates:
     - Each glyph's `bounds(GlyphId::new(glyph.id))` is a y-up box at the run's size. It becomes the box
       `(x + x_min, y − y_max)`–`(x + x_max, y − y_min)` about the glyph's origin `(glyph.x, glyph.y)`.
     - That box is widened by the run's `embolden` on each axis, mapped through its `glyph_transform` (about the
       origin) and its `transform`, and read as the axis-aligned bounding box.
     - The run's ink box is the union over its glyphs. A glyph with no outline (an empty box, a space) adds nothing.
     - A font skrifa cannot read, or a glyph id past its count, adds nothing.
   - No `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!` or `unreachable!`: a widget's font bytes are app data (CLAUDE.md, the no-panic
     invariant; security-plan · decision/no-panic-on-call-input). No glyph id, position or text leaves the module.
   - It opens no span and logs nothing (obs-plan · decision/canvas-read-opens-no-span; decision/driver-emits-no-event).
   - `canvas_lint_tests.rs` builds scenes of fills, clips, layers and masks with `anyrender::Scene` and no font. It
     asserts the clip box each push leaves and restores:
     - a clip narrows the box and its `PopLayer` restores the one beneath;
     - nested pushes intersect;
     - a push's transform maps its path before the box is taken;
     - a layer's and a mask's paths cut as a clip's does;
     - a pop on an empty stack is no panic.
     These run on the stack walk the module exposes to its child (`clip_boxes`, one box per command). The ink read is
     proven at step 5, where a real font is held.

3. **The lint reads each canvas's labels** (`packages/escher-driver/src/lint.rs`).
   - `Session::lint` keeps its order: it refuses `fonts-unavailable` first, then reads the snapshot and records its ids.
   - `findings` takes `&mut Harness<DioxusDocument>`. After `flatten`, it reads each entry's recorded scene through
     `Harness::canvas_scene(element)`, only for an entry with an element and a box with an area. `canvas_scene` is
     `None` for an element with no widget or an empty content box (architecture · contract/test-harness/canvas-scene).
     It then reads the rest through a shared borrow, as today.
   - A new `canvas_truncations(harness, entry, element, &Scene) -> Vec<Reason>`, beside `truncated`:
     - It reads the content box in CSS px: the element's client rect (`get_client_bounding_rect`) less its border
       and padding, from `final_layout`. That is the frame the widget paints in (architecture ·
       decision/custom-widget-content-box-paint; decision/widget-click-point-content-box).
     - It reads the viewport's scale (`get_viewport().scale_f64()`).
     - Each `Label`'s ink box and clip box map to CSS px by dividing by the scale and adding the content box's
       origin.
     - Its region is the content box, cut by the clip box where one stands, cut by `entry.region`.
     - A label whose ink box lies inside its region, to the existing 1/64 px `SLACK`, reads nothing. Any other label
       reads `Reason::Truncated { text: its ink box, visible: its intersection with the region }`. With no region
       (the element out of view) `visible` is `None`, as the DOM `truncated` reads.
   - `readings` gains these after the DOM `truncated` reading and before `contrast`, one finding per label in paint
     order. Findings stay in document order, then defect order, then the order found (architecture ·
     contract/lint-verb/finding; test-plan · contract/lint-findings/order).
   - The new code stays out of `findings`'s and `readings`'s bodies past one call each, under the dev-host
     cognitive-complexity ceiling of 15 (test-plan · decision/complexity-ceiling-host-only).
   - Doc comments that change, in the same words:
     - `Defect::Truncated` — «part of the element's laid-out text, or of a label its canvas widget paints, is cut
       from view»;
     - `Reason::Truncated.text` — «the box the laid-out lines take, or a canvas label's ink box»;
     - `Session::lint`'s list — its truncated bullet names the canvas label, its region and the ink box;
     - the stated limits (step 4) beside «Geometry only».

4. **The help, the crate doc and the capability statement** (`packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs`,
   `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs`, `docs/capabilities.md`).
   - The `lint` verb's help (`schema.rs:431`): `truncated` reads «part of its laid-out text, or of a label a canvas
     widget paints, cut from view». The `findings` field's help: `text` «the box the laid-out lines take, or a canvas
     label's ink box».
     - This is the program's own fixed text on the ratified carriers (architecture ·
       decision/fixed-program-text-on-carriers; security-plan · decision/mcp-listing-fixed-text).
     - `help` and the MCP listing read it from the one table, so the command line and MCP stay byte-equal
       (test-plan · contract/mcp-server/help).
   - The crate doc's lint paragraph (`lib.rs:84`) names the canvas label.
   - `docs/capabilities.md` §The visual lint (line 160):
     - one sentence on the canvas label, its region and its ink box, and that it rides `truncated` with no new word;
     - Circle Drawer at its four states reading no finding;
     - the witness `stand_canvas_lint` added to the section's witness line and to the closing check list.
     - Stated limits, written by hand (test-plan · decision/capability-claims-name-their-checks):
       - A pushed clip, layer or mask path is read as its bounding box, so a label outside a non-rectangular clip but
         inside its box reads clean.
       - A canvas under a transform reads its labels from its client rect's top left, unrotated and unscaled.
       - A glyph with no outline adds nothing to the ink box.
       - A canvas element the snapshot does not list is not linted.
     - The six-defect sentence, `README.md:53` and the `Defect::ALL` pin are unchanged (F1 A).

5. **The planted page and the stand reading** (new `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_lint.rs`; the Circle
   Drawer helpers moved to `tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs`).
   - **The move.** `circle_drawer`, `circles`, `carried`, `draw`, `reach` and `kinds` leave
     `stand_canvas_commands.rs` for `session_common`, the canvas's id with them as `CIRCLE_CANVAS`. Each body and
     panic message is unchanged, so `stand_canvas_commands` reads its 17-row table as before (test-plan ·
     decision/session-checks-share-one-module; decision/shared-stand-tables-in-one-module).
   - **The planted page** — one reader, so it stays in its check's file (test-plan · decision/shared-fixture-pages;
     decision/shared-fixtures-in-one-module).
     - A component booted alone through `stand::boot_alone` at `stand::options(incremental)`.
     - Its canvases are `object` elements. Each carries its id, `role: "group"` and an `aria-label`, so the snapshot
       lists it as Circle Drawer's canvas is listed. Each is `display: block; width: 200px; height: 40px`, stacked
       with no overlap.
     - Each carries a widget that shapes «Wide label» at 20 px from a context of the bundled DejaVu Sans alone
       (`blitz_dom::build_single_font_ctx(seven_guis::DEJAVU_SANS)`, as `stand_canvas_text`'s `BundledText` does).
       It draws the run with glyph origins on whole device px.
     - Numbered cases, a comment each (arch S2):
       1. `fx-inside` — the label wholly inside the content box: no finding.
       2. `fx-past-edge` — the label starting at x 150, running past the content box's right edge: `truncated`.
       3. `fx-past-clip` — a clip pushed at (0, 0)–(100, 40), the label at x 10 running past it inside the content
          box, then popped: `truncated`.
       4. `fx-after-pop` — a clip pushed at (0, 0)–(50, 40) and popped, then the label at x 10 inside the content
          box: no finding.
       5. `fx-ascent` — the label's baseline at y 10. Every glyph origin lies inside the content box, and its ascent
          passes the top edge: `truncated`, read by the ink box alone.
       6. `fx-in-clipped-box` — the canvas inside a 100 px wide `overflow: hidden` box, the label at x 110 inside
          the content box but past the clipping box: `clipped`, then `truncated`.
   - **Tests**, both layout modes each (arch S1; test-plan · decision/stand-checks-in-both-layout-modes):
     - `a_label_past_its_region_reads_truncated_on_the_planted_page`
       - First the fixture's precondition: each case's id is a snapshot node; its canvas summary reads one glyph run;
         and the fixture's origins box lies inside the content box for `fx-ascent` (arch S2).
       - Then the whole findings list equals a literal table: id, defect, and each box's four numbers. Its row count
         is asserted (5 rows: cases 2, 3 and 5 one each, case 6 two). Every number is pinned as measured in the
         engine at implement, never derived (test-plan · decision/expected-value-pinned-as-literal;
         decision/table-tests-count-their-rows).
       - Both modes read one table.
     - `the_lint_verb_answers_the_canvas_findings` — `Session::run` of the `lint` call answers `Outcome::Linted`.
       - Its `to_json` line holds the same findings, keyed `id`, `defect`, `bounds`, `text`, `visible` and no other.
       - It holds no glyph id, no glyph position and no text of the label: the line holds no «Wide» and keys from
         the closed set alone (security-plan · decision/canvas-content-crossing).
     - `circle_drawer_reads_no_canvas_finding_at_every_state` — for each of `boot`, `click`, `12`, `100`, through
       `reach`:
       - First the canvas summary's glyph-run count is read and pinned as a literal per state (measured;
         a label per circle is expected: 0 · 1 · 12 · 100). So a clean reading is never vacuous.
       - Then `Session::lint` returns no finding.
     - A failure message names a layout mode, a state or a row index only, never an argument value (test-plan ·
       decision/assertions-print-no-argument-value).
   - The target joins `stand-repeat` by the `stand_` glob. Its readers install no subscriber and print nothing
     (obs-plan · decision/checks-silent).

6. **The engine's label readings, recorded** — after step 5 reads green, /implement writes
   `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-24-canvas-lint/evidence/label-readings.md` (inputs#I3: the label readings are
   re-read in the engine, not from the model). It holds:
   - per stand state, the glyph runs read and the count of labels past their region, both from the engine (the
     `stand_canvas_lint` reading) — predicted 0 · 1 · 12 · 100 runs and 0 past at each state, to be measured;
   - the planted table's measured boxes as pinned.
   The research model's other counts — labels past their own circle, labels overlapping — measure F2 B and F4 B,
   which this chunk does not build. They are named there as not re-measured, never restated as readings.

7. **Controls**, after the steps read green: one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries (test-plan ·
   decision/mutation-controlled-tests; gate-contract.md §Control). Each names the text its edit removes and its case
   by test name, and each enters with the red reading it must produce. All but C5 fire on the `stand_canvas_lint`
   entry, so no earlier target is passed over (test-plan · decision/control-leaves-earlier-target-green).
   - **C1 — the ink box.**
     - Edit: `ink` returns the glyph origins' box in place of the outline bounds.
     - Case: `a_label_past_its_region_reads_truncated_on_the_planted_page`.
     - Red reading: `fx-ascent`'s row is missing, the table reading 4 rows of 5.
   - **C2 — the pushed clip.**
     - Edit: `labels` gives every run the clip `None`.
     - Case: the same.
     - Red reading: `fx-past-clip`'s row is missing.
   - **C3 — the element's clip region.**
     - Edit: `canvas_truncations` does not cut by `entry.region`.
     - Case: the same.
     - Red reading: `fx-in-clipped-box` reads `clipped` alone, its `truncated` row missing.
   - **C4 — the pop.**
     - Edit: `PopLayer` leaves the stack as it is.
     - Case: the same.
     - Red reading: `fx-after-pop` reads a `truncated` row the table does not hold.
   - **C5 — the stack walk's pop, in the unit tests.**
     - Edit: the same as C4.
     - Fired on: the escher-driver unit entry.
     - Case: the unit test asserting a pop restores the box beneath.
     - Red reading: that case `failed`.
   - **C6 — the lint joins the canvas.**
     - Edit: `readings` no longer chains `canvas_truncations`.
     - Case: `a_label_past_its_region_reads_truncated_on_the_planted_page`.
     - Red reading: the page reads 1 row (`fx-in-clipped-box`'s `clipped`) of 5.
   - Each control's line, `holds` with its case read `failed`, is recorded in
     `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-24-canvas-lint/evidence/`. A `DOES NOT HOLD` is a stop that widens the case, never
     a dropped control.
   - The tool makes its own clone under `~/.cache/andromeda-control/` and removes it itself. No plan step deletes a
     worktree or a build directory (inputs#I3).
- `packages/escher-driver/src/canvas_lint.rs` — the label reading: each glyph run's ink box and the clip box its pushes leave
- `packages/escher-driver/src/canvas_lint_tests.rs` — the stack walk's unit tests, a `#[path]` child
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_lint.rs` — the planted page, the `lint` verb's answer, Circle Drawer clean at four states
- `packages/escher-driver/Cargo.toml` — `skrifa = { workspace = true }`
- `Cargo.lock` — escher-driver's dependency list gains `"skrifa"`, no package added
- `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs` — the module and the lint paragraph of the crate doc
- `packages/escher-driver/src/lint.rs` — `findings` reads each canvas's scene; `canvas_truncations`; the doc comments
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` — the `lint` verb's help and its `findings` field's help
- `docs/capabilities.md` — §The visual lint: the canvas label, its limits, its witness
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs` — Circle Drawer's helpers, moved in unchanged
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_commands.rs` — the moved helpers read from `session_common`
The gates:
- the lock entries;
- the `--locked` workspace build;
- escher-driver's unit tests;
- the new stand target;
- the blitz-tests companions the diff moves;
- seven_guis' four process checks;
- the capability-statement pin;
- the pre-push gate (`fast`);

- the `doc` leg. The chunk edits public doc comments (`Defect`, `Reason`, `Session::lint`, the crate doc), and `fast`
  runs no rustdoc (test-plan · decision/doc-leg-gates-public-doc-edits);
- the `audit` leg. escher-driver takes a dependency, and the fast leg runs no audit;
- `stand-repeat`. The new target is a `stand_` file and runs by its glob.
What is absent:

- No boot-path touchpoint changes a binary's start: `session_host.rs` is untouched. `cli_commands`, `mcp_server`,
  `host_log` and `mcp_log` drive both binaries' roles and stand in for the smoke.
- There is no live leg: no cold-agent run.
- There is no headful self-verify harness in this project.

- The coverage leg is not run locally. CI's coverage job reads escher-driver's 97 % floor on the pushed tree, and the
  CI read below asserts green over it.
The controls are step 7's one-shot runs, each with its red reading.

An acceptance reads CI: the windows and macOS test legs hold the planted table's literals and the stand's clean
reading. The diff adds no OS-conditional site. The `ci.py` entry's note names what each OS leg witnesses.

# Canvas lint — the take-up's forks

Chunk `2026-11-24-canvas-lint` (working entry chk-mt7d55q7, «Canvas lint — lint-like checks inside a canvas, a label
overflowing its region among them (v040-10)»), stopped at P4 before any plan was written, on the operator's directive

`doc:2026-11-24-canvas-lint/scope` rev 3; research `doc:2026-11-24-canvas-lint/research` rev 1.

Five forks: one is the founder's (F1), four are the operator's (F2–F5).

Measurement basis used below:
- **Sweeps:** `git grep` over packages, tests, examples, docs and README.md, recorded in research `## Sweeps`.
- **Label positions:** a model of DejaVu Sans' digit metrics over the stand's fixed circle sequence: advance
  1303/2048 em and line height (1901+483)/2048 em at 12 px, on a 700 × 400 canvas. It is a model, not an engine
  reading; implement re-reads it in the engine.

---

## F1 — Which carrier a canvas finding rides — **the founder's**

**What crosses.** A finding about a canvas's painted content:
- the canvas element's stable id;
- a closed defect word;
- numbers: the label's extent box and the visible part of its region, in CSS px.

The extent box is new: it is derived from glyph positions and the font's advances. Today a canvas answer carries
only each glyph run's origins box (`canvas.rs:408-417`).

On a carrier, this content reaches every MCP client. The cold-agent pipe already allows both `lint` and `canvas`
(`scripts/cold-agent.sh:54`), so a live run would carry it on to the model provider.

**The rules it meets.**
- **Why it is the founder's:** the v040-10 requirement itself says «what it may carry to a provider is the
  founder's fork» (`cap:escher-0.4.0/v040-10`, per intent §6).
- Playbook pattern `rul-izni57qv` (Boundary widening, `escalate`): a validated surface carrying a new class of
  content.
- The founder's rule of 2026-10-10 (`decision/boundary-widening-rule`): a new closed-value field inside a ratified
  carrier is no widening. Under it, option B's word and option C's field alone would not widen. What they would
  newly carry is canvas-derived geometry, and v040-10 reserves that question to him.
- Precedent: the founder's own rulings on the visual lint — F1 «Новая команда lint» (a verb rather than in process
  only) and F2 «Без поля» (no added field). Both were recorded at 2026-10-20-select-by-id.
- `decision/canvas-content-crossing` (ratified): canvas content crosses as pixels and as the canvas answer, never as
  a glyph id, glyph position, text, font bytes or family name.

**Options, each with its measured cost.**
- **A. Reuse the `truncated` word in the `lint` answer.** The canvas element reads `truncated`, its reason
  `text` = the label's extent and `visible` = the part of it inside its region.
  - Closed sets: no new defect word, no new reason key; the defect set stays six.
  - Sites that move:
    - the `lint` help text (`schema.rs:431`, fixed program text);
    - `docs/capabilities.md:160`;
    - the `escher-driver` lib doc (`lib.rs:84`);
    - `lint.rs` itself.
  - What stays the same:
    - `README.md:53`;
    - the `Defect::ALL` pin (`lint.rs:573`);
    - the six `contract/lint-defects/*` rows.
  - Committed tables and checks: 0 move. None of the seven served tasks paints a canvas, and Circle Drawer is
    served by no `escher-session` role (`contract/headless-stand/boot`), so `stand_cross_os_readings`' lint digests,
    the two committed Counter checks and the `host_log`/`mcp_log` needle reads are unchanged.
  - Rows owed at the wrap: `contract/lint-verb/truncated` and `decision/canvas-content-crossing` (plus the lint
    carrier rows in security and obs), amended to say that a canvas's labels are read.
- **B. A new closed defect word in the `lint` answer** (e.g. `label-overflow`), with `truncated`'s reason keys.
  - The defect set goes from six to seven, so 7 of the 11 sweep hits move: `README.md:53`,
    `docs/capabilities.md:160`, `lib.rs:84`, `lint.rs:1`, `lint.rs:573` (the `Defect::ALL` pin), `schema.rs:431`,
    `stand_lint.rs:1`.
  - Contract rows that move: `contract/lint-verb/defects` («closed at six») and the six `contract/lint-defects/*`
